paragraphs.source_en: With Mr. Tofu’s visit, while I cannot say that every eccentric who frequents my master’s house has now been gathered in, at least a considerable number of guests have assembled, enough to console my loneliness. If I were still to complain that this was not enough, I should be quite ungrateful. Had ill luck caused me to be kept in some other household, I might have gone through my whole life without ever encountering even one of these gentlemen. Fortunately, as a cat in the service of Mr. Kushami, attending morning and evening before his tiger-skin seat, I am able to behold the conduct of such champions as Mr. Kushami himself, not to mention Meitei, Kangetsu, and even Tofu, men so valiant that one could scarcely find their like in all Tokyo. That I now have the chance to lie there and watch their every gesture is, for me, a once-in-a-thousand-years piece of good fortune. Moreover, thanks to these gentlemen, I can forget the misery of being wrapped in fur in this fierce heat and pass half a day most amusingly; for that I am deeply grateful. Since so many of them had gathered, I was sure something out of the ordinary must occur, and expecting some fine spectacle, I hid behind the sliding doors of the parlor and waited reverently to observe their bearing, words, and deeds.
